teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Define the normal distribution.
Let $X$ denote the weight in kilograms of a 16-year-old boy in Jimpuri:
$$X \sim \mathrm{N}(61.4, 12.3^2)$$
with mean $\mu = 61.4$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 12.3$.

Step 2: Standardize the value $65$ kg:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{65 - 61.4}{12.3} = \frac{3.6}{12.3} \approx 0.2927$$

Step 3: Compute the upper tail probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 65) = \mathrm{P}(Z > 0.293) = 1 - \Phi(0.293)$$
From the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(0.29) = 0.6141, \quad \text{difference for } 3 = 12 \implies \Phi(0.293) = 0.6153$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 65) = 1 - 0.6153 = 0.3847 \approx 0.385$$

hints: Express this as $\mathrm{P}(X < k) - \mathrm{P}(X < 65) = 0.25$, and use $\mathrm{P}(X < 65) = 0.6153$ from part (i).
Find $z$ such that $\Phi(z) = 0.8653$ and solve $\frac{k - 61.4}{12.3} = z$ for $k$.
walkthrough:
Use the interval probability equation:
$$\mathrm{P}(65 < X < k) = 0.25$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X < k) - \mathrm{P}(X < 65) = 0.25$$

Find the corresponding standardized value from the normal table:
$$\Phi(z) = 0.8653 \implies z = 1.105$$

ai_rubric.Using Inverse Normal Values: Finds Phi(z) = 0.8653, z = 1.105, and solves for k = 75.0 kg.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up the probability statement.
We are given that $25\%$ of boys have weights between $65\text{ kg}$ and $k\text{ kg}$:
$$\mathrm{P}(65 < X < k) = 0.25$$
Rewrite in terms of cumulative probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < k) - \mathrm{P}(X < 65) = 0.25$$

Step 2: Use the cumulative probability from part (i):
From part (i), $\mathrm{P}(X > 65) = 0.3847$, so $\mathrm{P}(X < 65) = 1 - 0.3847 = 0.6153$.
$$\mathrm{P}(X < k) = 0.25 + 0.6153 = 0.8653$$

Step 3: Look up $z$ in the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(z) = 0.8653$$
From the table:
$$\Phi(1.10) = 0.8643, \quad \text{difference for } 5 = 10 \implies z = 1.105$$

Step 4: Solve for $k$:
$$\frac{k - \mu}{\sigma} = 1.105$$
$$\frac{k - 61.4}{12.3} = 1.105$$
$$k - 61.4 = 1.105 \times 12.3 = 13.5915$$
$$k = 61.4 + 13.5915 = 74.9915 \approx 75.0\text{ kg}$$

hints: Use the upper condition: 1% weigh more than 97.2 kg $\implies \Phi(z_1) = 0.99 \implies z_1 = 2.326$.
Use the lower condition: 33% weigh less than 55.2 kg $\implies \Phi(z_2) = 0.33 \implies z_2 = -0.44$.
Set up the two simultaneous equations: $\frac{97.2 - \mu}{\sigma} = 2.326$ and $\frac{55.2 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.44$, and solve for $\mu$ and $\sigma$.
walkthrough:
Set up the standardization equation for the upper percentile:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y > 97.2) = 0.01 \implies \Phi(z_1) = 0.99 \implies z_1 = 2.326$$
$$\frac{97.2 - \mu}{\sigma} = 2.326 \implies 97.2 - \mu = 2.326\sigma \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

Set up the standardization equation for the lower percentile:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y < 55.2) = 0.33 \implies \Phi(z_2) = 0.33 \implies z_2 = -0.44$$
$$\frac{55.2 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.44 \implies 55.2 - \mu = -0.44\sigma \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Subtract equation (2) from equation (1) to eliminate $\mu$:
$$(97.2 - \mu) - (55.2 - \mu) = 2.326\sigma - (-0.44\sigma)$$
$$42.0 = 2.766\sigma \implies \sigma = \frac{42.0}{2.766} \approx 15.184 \approx 15.2\text{ kg}$$

Substitute $\sigma$ back to find $\mu$:
$$\mu = 55.2 + 0.44(15.184) = 55.2 + 6.681 = 61.881 \approx 61.9\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Mean: } 61.9\text{ kg}, \quad \text{Standard deviation: } 15.2\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Normal Distribution Parameters: Sets up simultaneous equations with z = 2.326 and z = -0.44, solving to get mu = 61.9 kg and sigma = 15.2 kg.
ai_rubric.Using Inverse Normal Values: Identifies z1 = 2.326 from 0.99 and z2 = -0.44 from 0.33.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Translate the percentage statements for Brigville into probability statements.
Let $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ be the weights of boys in Brigville.
- Condition 1: $1\%$ weigh more than $97.2\text{ kg}$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y > 97.2) = 0.01 \implies \mathrm{P}(Y < 97.2) = 0.99$$
From the critical value table:
$$z_1 = 2.326$$

- Condition 2: $33\%$ weigh less than $55.2\text{ kg}$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y < 55.2) = 0.33$$
Because this is below the median ($0.33 < 0.50$), $z_2$ is negative:
$$\Phi(-z_2) = 1 - 0.33 = 0.67$$
From normal tables, $\Phi(0.44) = 0.6700$, so:
$$z_2 = -0.44$$

Step 2: Formulate the standardization equations:
$$\frac{97.2 - \mu}{\sigma} = 2.326 \implies 97.2 - \mu = 2.326\sigma \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$
$$\frac{55.2 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.44 \implies 55.2 - \mu = -0.44\sigma \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Step 3: Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1 to eliminate $\mu$:
$$97.2 - 55.2 = 2.326\sigma - (-0.44\sigma)$$
$$42.0 = 2.766\sigma$$
$$\sigma = \frac{42.0}{2.766} \approx 15.18438 \approx 15.2\text{ kg}$$

Step 4: Solve for $\mu$ using Equation 2:
$$\mu = 55.2 + 0.44\sigma = 55.2 + 0.44(15.18438) = 55.2 + 6.6811 = 61.8811 \approx 61.9\text{ kg}$$
